record.context_brief: Proportional deterioration with precedence and weighted completion
record.original_question: Given n jobs to be scheduled on a single machine with arbitrary precedence constraints represented by an acyclic directed graph, where job j has proportional time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = b_j t when it starts at time t, job j has weight w_j, and C_j is its completion time, determine the computational complexity of minimizing the total weighted completion time sum_j w_j C_j. Is this precedence-constrained problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or is there a polynomial-time algorithm?

evidence.quote: 1|p j=b j t, prec|P w j C j

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem with proportional time-dependent processing times. We are given a set of n jobs {1, 2, ..., n} to be scheduled (without preemption) on a single machine that can process at most one job at a time. Each job j has:
- a positive deterioration rate b_j > 0, so that if job j is started at time t > 0 its processing time equals p_j(t) = b_j · t (the machine starts at some fixed time t_0 > 0);
- a positive weight w_j > 0;
- precedence constraints described by an arbitrary acyclic directed graph G on the job set: an arc (i, j) means that job i must be completed before job j may start.

Let C_j denote the completion time of job j in a feasible schedule. The objective is to find a feasible schedule (a linear extension of G respected by the machine) that minimizes the total weighted completion time
  Σ_{j=1}^{n} w_j C_j.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem. Specifically, is the problem NP-hard (at least in the ordinary sense), or does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm solving it to optimality?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive complexity classification (polynomial-time algorithm or NP-hardness proof) for the single-machine proportional-deterioration problem with arbitrary precedence constraints and weighted completion-time objective. The problem appears in surveys of time-dependent scheduling as an open complexity question; no resolution could be verified from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Weighted sum of completion times
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses complexity of weighted completion time scheduling with precedence constraints in classical and time-dependent settings.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on weighted-completion-time scheduling do not list a known polynomial algorithm or NP-hardness proof for the proportional-deterioration variant with arbitrary precedence.
